summary: 3 important, 3 nit, 0 pre-existing (1 still open from earlier rounds).

findings.title: Queued compile_commands regeneration is dropped when generate() is called with nil targets
findings.body: While a run is in progress, generate() stores `ws.compdb_again = targets`. The BUILD-file save path calls generate(ws) with targets == nil (init.lua:135), so compdb_again becomes nil and the re-run check at compdb.lua:140 is falsy. A nil call also overwrites targets queued earlier by :BazelGcc compdb <targets>.
findings.failure_scenario: Save BUILD.bazel twice while aquery runs: the second request is lost, and compile_commands.json reflects the state before the second edit until the next save.
findings.suggested_fix: Queue with a boolean plus targets, e.g. ws.compdb_again = { targets = targets }, and check that table.

findings.title: curl | sh installers mask download failures, so the image builds without starship or claude
findings.body: The starship install (Dockerfile:45) and the Claude install (Dockerfile:57) use `curl -fsSL URL | sh|bash` as plain RUN steps under /bin/sh (dash) with no pipefail. If curl fails (network error, HTTP 4xx/5xx), the downstream shell reads empty stdin and exits 0, so the layer succeeds and the tool is silently missing. post-create.sh:36 only echoes 'not found' for a missing claude. The NodeSource layer (Dockerfile:21) has the same pipe, but there the following apt-get/npm steps fail loudly, so only the masking pattern applies to it.
findings.failure_scenario: A transient failure fetching https://claude.ai/install.sh or https://starship.rs/install.sh makes curl exit non-zero; sh receives empty stdin and exits 0, so the image builds. The container then has no claude / no starship prompt, with no build error. Reproduced: `sh -c 'curl -fsSL http://127.0.0.1:9/install.sh | sh -s -- -y'; echo exit=$?` -> exit=0.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]` before these steps, or download to a file first and run it; run `command -v claude` / `command -v starship` afterwards.

findings.title: A build that produced no BEP file wipes the stored Bazel/BUILD diagnostics and reports a misleading result
findings.body: bep.read (bep.lua:20-22) returns an empty result when the BEP file is missing, for example when bazel fails before it opens --build_event_json_file (bad flag in build_args, startup failure) or is interrupted before the file exists. finish() does not check res.code or whether any event was read. It unconditionally calls store.set_bazel(ws, update.bazel) (build.lua:84), which replaces ALL stored bazel diagnostics (store.lua:73-80), then store.save() persists the empty set and store.publish clears the buffers. Existing BUILD-file errors disappear even though no analysis ran, and the notification reads FAILED with 0 error(s). The state heals on the next build that reports the analysis errors again.
findings.failure_scenario: A BUILD file has an analysis error shown as a diagnostic. A later bazel invocation fails before writing the BEP (for example a bad flag in build_args). finish() runs with empty events, set_bazel({}) clears and persists the BUILD diagnostics, and the user sees 'FAILED ... 0 error(s)'.
findings.suggested_fix: In finish(), when the BEP file is missing or empty and res.code ~= 0, skip set_bazel/set_action, keep the old store and only report the failure. Have bep.read return nil, err when io.open fails.

findings.title: Owner query interpolates the file label unquoted into a bazel query expression
findings.body: The expression is built with ('kind(rule, same_pkg_direct_rdeps(%s))'):format(label), where the label is '//pkg:name' with the raw file name (workspace.lua). Bazel query treats space, ',', '(' and ')' as syntax and '+' as the union operator, so a source file whose name contains one of them produces a query error. The failure is surfaced as a WARN ('owners query failed') and the fallback is used: //pkg:all by default, or nothing when fallback = none. compdb.lua:126 joins targets with ' + ' unquoted as well, but its inputs are configured or pinned labels.
findings.failure_scenario: Saving lib/my file.cc or lib/a+b.cc runs an unparsable query (reproduced with bazel 9: "syntax error at 'file.cc ) )'" and "couldn't determine target from filename 'b.cc'"). Every save warns and builds //pkg:all; with fallback = none the file never builds on save.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the label in double quotes with embedded quotes escaped (same_pkg_direct_rdeps("%s")), and quote each target in compdb.lua as well.

findings.title: In-flight owners query can repopulate ws.owners after a BUILD-file save cleared it
findings.body: init.lua:134 resets ws.owners = {} when a BUILD file is saved. An async bazel query started earlier (build.lua:41) writes ws.owners[file] = targets (build.lua:58) when it returns, with no check that the cache was invalidated in the meantime. The query ran against the pre-edit BUILD file and its result is served from cache (build.lua:22-23) until the next BUILD save.
findings.failure_scenario: Save foo.cc, which starts the owners query. Before it returns, edit BUILD to move foo.cc to another target and save. The stale query completes and caches the old target list; later saves of foo.cc build the wrong target until the next BUILD save.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a generation counter to ws that is bumped on invalidation, and only cache a result if the generation is unchanged.

findings.title: store.save writes the state file non-atomically and unchecked; stale action entries are never pruned
findings.body: save() (store.lua:45-49) opens the per-workspace state file with 'w', which truncates it, then writes and closes without checking results; there is no temp-file-and-rename, unlike compdb.lua:150-158 in the same plugin. A crash or full disk mid-write, or a second Neovim instance loading while the file is truncated, leaves/reads truncated JSON; ensure() (store.lua:34) swallows the decode error with pcall and starts empty, so the cached-action warnings the header comment promises to keep across restarts are silently lost. Two instances on one workspace are last-writer-wins on the whole file. Separately, set_action only replaces keys present in the current build, and nothing prunes actions whose targets were deleted or renamed; those entries keep feeding quickfix and the counts until :BazelGcc clear.
findings.failure_scenario: Neovim is killed or the disk fills during save. The next session loads a truncated file, the decode fails, and every cached-action warning is dropped without notice until those actions re-run. After a target is deleted or renamed, its old errors stay in quickfix and the counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Write to a temp file and fs_rename it over the state file, as compdb.lua does; check write/close results and notify on failure. Prune actions whose primary output or source file no longer exists.

resolved.title: consult-find-args is set to an fd command, but consult-find appends find-style predicates
consult-projectile-mode does not exist; :config calls an undefined function
claudecode terminal_cmd hardcodes the macOS Homebrew path /opt/homebrew/bin/claude
Busy flag ws.running is set only inside the async workspace.info callback, so concurrent builds can start
bazel info: a synchronous vim.system spawn failure leaves ws.info_waiters set forever
Stowed global gitconfig hardcodes the devpod credential helper and a fixed port
Failed bazel owners query is silently cached as the fallback result
compile_commands.json write: assert(io.open) and unchecked write/rename results
qf_items sort comparator is not a strict weak ordering, so warnings and notes interleave
